Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, and suppose $X$ has a finite cover by $T$-invariant affine open subvarieties. Use rational coefficients. Let $K=(S^1)^r$ be the maximal compact subgroup of $T$, and use the product right Milnor model $E_K=(E_{S^1})^r$, $B_K=E_K/K=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$. The inclusion $K\subset T$ gives the same topological Borel construction up to homotopy. For each algebraic character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, let $L_\chi=E_K\times_K\mathbb C_{\chi|_K}\to B_K$, with right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_\chi=c_1(L_\chi)$. For the coordinate characters $\chi_i$ and $u_i=u_{\chi_i}$, the coefficient ring is $R_T=H^*(B_K;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, with $|u_i|=2$ and $u_\chi=\sum_i n_i u_i$ for $\chi(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$. Let $S_T$ be the multiplicative set consisting of $1$ and finite products of $u_\chi$ for nontrivial $\chi$.

Let $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{T,c}(X;\mathbb Q)}(\mathbb Q_X,\omega_X^T[-j])$, where $\omega_X^T$ is the normalized equivariant dualizing object whose restriction is the ordinary dualizing object $\omega_X$, without a quotient-stack dimension shift. Equivalently, this is the stable value in degree $j$ of $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{j+2rm}(X_m;\mathbb Q)$, where $U_m=(\mathbb C^{m+1}\setminus\{0\})^r$ has the free right scalar $T$-action, $X_m=(U_m\times X)/T$ uses $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$, and the supplied bounded-Hom comparison is taken in its stable range. The ring $R_T$ acts by pullback from $B_K$ and cap product. For an $R_T$-module $M$, $S_T^{-1}M$ consists of fractions $m/s$ with $m\in M$, $s\in S_T$, and $m/s=m'/s'$ exactly when some $t\in S_T$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$; addition and scalar multiplication are the induced fraction operations. Proper equivariant maps induce degree-preserving pushforwards, invariant open inclusions induce Borel–Moore restrictions, and a smooth pure $d$-dimensional complex variety has its complex-oriented fundamental class $[X]_T$ in degree $2d$. For $r=0$, $R_T=\mathbb Q$ and $S_T=\{1\}$.

Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act on a smooth separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $F=X^T$ be proper, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$, $p_F:F\to\mathrm{pt}$, and $S_T$ the character multiplicative set. By the finite-affine-atlas concentration isomorphism, $i_*:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F;\mathbb Q)\to S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)$ is invertible. Define the intrinsic localized pushforward
$$
p^{\mathrm{loc}}_*:=p_{F*}\circ(i_*)^{-1}:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb Q),
$$
where $p_{F*}$ is the genuine proper Borel–Moore pushforward. For a homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^q(X;\mathbb Q)$ and smooth complex dimension $d$, an allowed insertion is $\alpha\cap[X]_T\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_{2d-q}(X;\mathbb Q)$; the fundamental class $[X]_T$ is the complex-oriented class, not the cohomological unit $1\in H_T^0(X;\mathbb Q)$. This construction does not define an ordinary pushforward along a nonproper map $X\to\mathrm{pt}$.

Let $G$ be a complex affine algebraic group acting algebraically on a classical
variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-rational-action-on-affine-variety]]). A $G$-invariant morphism
$\pi:X\to Y$ is a **categorical quotient** if every $G$-invariant morphism
$f:X\to Z$ of classical varieties factors uniquely as $f=\varphi\circ\pi$ with
$\varphi:Y\to Z$ a morphism.

It is a **geometric quotient** (Brion Definition 1.18) if

(i) $\pi$ is surjective and its fibres are exactly the $G$-orbits,

(ii) a subset $U\subseteq Y$ is open if and only if $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is open in
$X$, and

(iii) for every open $U\subseteq Y$ the pullback of regular functions is an
isomorphism $\mathcal O_Y(U)\to\mathcal O_X(\pi^{-1}(U))^G$ onto the
$G$-invariant regular functions on the preimage.

A geometric quotient is a categorical quotient and is unique up to unique
isomorphism; when it exists its underlying topological space is the orbit space
$X/G$ with the quotient topology. For an affine $G$-variety $X$ whose invariant
algebra $\mathbb C[X]^G$ is finitely generated, the affine model is the morphism
$\pi:X\to X/\!/G:=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[X]^G$ induced by the inclusion
$\mathbb C[X]^G\subseteq\mathbb C[X]$. For a reductive $G$, the theorem below
proves this finite generation and makes the model a categorical quotient with
one closed orbit in each fibre
([[thm-invariant-ring-finite-generation-and-affine-categorical-quotient]]).

**Why a geometric quotient is categorical.** Let $\pi:X\to Y$ satisfy (i)–(iii)
and let $f:X\to Z$ be a $G$-invariant morphism to a classical variety $Z$. By
(i) two points of a fibre of $\pi$ lie in one orbit, on which $f$ is constant,
so $f$ factors through a unique set map $\bar f:Y\to Z$. For $W\subseteq Z$
open, $\pi^{-1}(\bar f^{-1}(W))=f^{-1}(W)$ is open in $X$ by continuity of $f$,
so $\bar f^{-1}(W)$ is open in $Y$ by (ii): $\bar f$ is continuous. If $V$ is an
affine chart of $Z$ with coordinates $s$ and $U:=\bar f^{-1}(V)$, then
$s\circ f$ is a $G$-invariant regular function on $\pi^{-1}(U)$, hence by (iii)
is the pullback along $\pi$ of a unique regular function on $U$; that function
is $s\circ\bar f$. Since this holds for every coordinate $s$ of an affine chart,
$\bar f$ is a morphism
([[def-classical-affine-variety-morphism]],
[[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and local
agreement of the resulting morphisms on overlapping charts gives a morphism
$Y\to Z$. Surjectivity in (i) makes the factorisation unique. If also
$\pi':X\to Y'$ is a categorical quotient, the universal property applied to
$\pi'$ and to $\pi$ yields morphisms $\varphi:Y\to Y'$ with $\varphi\pi=\pi'$
and $\psi:Y'\to Y$ with $\psi\pi'=\pi$; then $(\varphi\psi)\pi'=\pi'$ and
$(\psi\varphi)\pi=\pi$, so uniqueness of the factorisation of $\pi'$ through
$\pi'$ and of $\pi$ through $\pi$ forces $\varphi\psi=\operatorname{id}_{Y'}$
and $\psi\varphi=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Thus categorical and geometric
quotients are unique up to unique isomorphism, and for a geometric quotient
(i)–(ii) say exactly that the underlying map is the quotient map of the orbit
equivalence relation with the quotient topology.

**Conventions.** This is the classical notion of Brion Definition 1.18 and the
paragraph after Theorem 1.24. The scheme-theoretic fppf quotient sheaf on the
AG-ACT-1 page is a different object and is not identified with this classical
notion here. In the classical register, $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a finitely
generated reduced complex algebra denotes its associated affine variety of
complex closed points with the classical regular-function sheaf; no
identification with the space of every scheme prime is used. For empty $X$ the
coordinate algebra is zero and its quotient is empty; finite generation and the
universal properties below are then immediate and fibre assertions are vacuous.
The definition itself uses no Axiom of Choice; the finite-generation theorem
referred to above inherits AC from its own named suppliers, so consumers of that
theorem carry AC, while nothing in this definition does.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard bases. Let $X$ be the stable locus in the complex ADHM equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, where $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$, and stability means that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$. The action $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ of $GL(V)$ on $X$ is free and proper. Its orbit quotient with quotient topology is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension $2kN$, with tangent space $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$ for the infinitesimal ADHM deformation maps.

For $k>0$, a word frame $C(x)$ is a matrix whose columns are $k$ fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard framing basis vectors. The opens $U_C=\{x:\det C(x)\ne0\}$ cover $X$; words of length at most $k-1$ suffice. Each slice $S_C=\{x\in U_C:C(x)=I_V\}$ gives quotient coordinates, with $GL(V)\times S_C\to U_C$ a biholomorphism. Slice changes are holomorphic, in fact given by matrix inversion and polynomial operations on their domains. The quotient is also a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite $T$-invariant affine atlas of these slices, and the map from $X$ is a geometric quotient in the regular-function sense.

Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, with $h$ acting on the $\alpha$th standard framing vector by $e_\alpha^{-1}$. This descends to a smooth holomorphic action. At any fixed quotient point represented by $x$, there is a unique $g(t)\in GL(V)$ with $t\cdot x=g(t)\cdot x$. If column $\ell$ of $C(x)$ uses framing color $\alpha_\ell$ and contains $a_\ell,b_\ell$ letters $B_1,B_2$, then

$$g(t)=C(x)\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})C(x)^{-1}.$$

Thus the lift is a smooth character representation, without assuming Zariski density or a GIT linearization theorem. For $k=0$ the quotient is a point and these matrices and tangent spaces have their empty-dimensional interpretations. No correspondence with a real moment-map quotient, sheaf moduli or ASD connections is asserted.

If $X$ and $Y$ are smooth left $G$-manifolds, a smooth map $f:X\to Y$ is
**$G$-equivariant** if

$$f(g\cdot x)=g\cdot f(x)$$

for all $g\in G$ and $x\in X$.

A smooth vector bundle $\pi:E\to M$ is a **$G$-equivariant vector bundle**
if $G$ acts smoothly on $E$ and $M$, the projection is equivariant, and each
map $E_x\to E_{g\cdot x}$, $v\mapsto g\cdot v$, is linear. Thus the
total-space action is jointly smooth and consists of fibrewise-linear bundle
maps covering the base action.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, and use $E_T=(E_{S^1})^r$, the product of the right Milnor join models, with $BT=E_T/T$. For the $i$th coordinate character $\chi_i([t_1,\ldots,t_r])=\exp(2\pi i t_i)$, let $L_i=E_T\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_i}$ be the associated complex line bundle over $BT$, with the right diagonal equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi_i(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_i=c_1(L_i)\in H^2(BT;\mathbb Q)$. Then
$$
BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r,\qquad H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2.
$$
Every smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$ is uniquely $\chi_{\mathbf n}([t])=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i n_it_i)$ for $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb Z^r$, and its associated line satisfies $c_1(L_{\chi_{\mathbf n}})=\sum_i n_i u_i$. In particular a nontrivial character has a nonzero degree-two class. For each $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, $H_q(BT;k)$ is finite-dimensional in every degree $q$. For $r=0$, $BT$ is a point and its rational cohomology is $\mathbb Q$.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. For $r>0$, let

$$S^4_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^5:\sum_{j=1}^5y_j^2=r^2\}$$

with its standard orientation, round metric, scalar curvature $12/r^2$, and standard spin structure. The radius has dimension $[r]=\mathrm{mass}^{-1}$. In stereographic length coordinates $x^\mu$, $\mu=1,\ldots,4$, use

$$ds^2=\frac{\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2}{(1+x^2/(4r^2))^2},\qquad x^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2.$$

Let $G=U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak u(2)=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^\dagger=-X\}$ and positive invariant form $(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}(XY)$. A gauge sector is a smooth right principal $U(2)$ bundle $P\to S^4_r$ up to smooth bundle isomorphism, with a smooth connection $A$ and curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ in a local trivialization. Fields in the adjoint representation are smooth sections of the associated adjoint bundle. This postulate does not classify the bundle sectors.

Use Pestun's dimensional-reduction notation only as a field and spinor convention: $M,N=0,\ldots,9$ are ten-dimensional indices, $\mu=1,\ldots,4$ are the S4 coordinate indices, $A\in\{0,5,\ldots,9\}$ labels the six reduced scalars, and $i,j,k=5,\ldots,8$ label the four hypermultiplet scalars. Independently, $a,b=1,\ldots,7$ label localization auxiliaries $K_a$ and their background spinors $\nu_a$; these labels are not reduced spacetime directions. Write the reduced ten-dimensional connection as $A_M=(A_\mu,\Phi_A)$; $\Phi_0,\Phi_9$ and the fermion components in the $\Gamma_{5678}=+1$ multiplet form the N=2 vector multiplet, while $\Phi_5,\ldots,\Phi_8$ and the complementary fermion components form one adjoint hypermultiplet. There is no other matter. The ten-dimensional indices do not enlarge the four-dimensional spacetime.

In the source's reduced $(9,1)$ Clifford convention, let $g_{MN}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\ldots,1)$ and let $\gamma^M$ be the $32\times32$ matrices satisfying $\gamma^M\gamma^N+\gamma^N\gamma^M=2g^{MN}I$. Their two chiral blocks are $\Gamma^M:S^+\to S^-$ and $\widetilde\Gamma^M:S^-\to S^+$, satisfying $\Gamma^{(M}\widetilde\Gamma^{N)}=\widetilde\Gamma^{(M}\Gamma^{N)}=g^{MN}I$, where parentheses and brackets denote symmetrization and antisymmetrization with factor $1/2$. Set $\Gamma^{MN}=\widetilde\Gamma^{[M}\Gamma^{N]}$ on $S^+$ and $\widetilde\Gamma^{MN}=\Gamma^{[M}\widetilde\Gamma^{N]}$ on $S^-$, as in Pestun Appendix A (A.7). The blocks are symmetric and $(\Gamma^{MN})^{\mathsf T}=-\widetilde\Gamma^{MN}$. A bilinear $\zeta B\chi$ means $\zeta^{\mathsf T}B\chi$ in this basis, with no Hermitian conjugation; the background spinors commute and dynamical fermions are odd. The spinor $\Psi$ and supersymmetry parameter $\epsilon$ are chiral Majorana-Weyl spinors in this reduced convention; after Euclidean continuation $\Psi$ is complex and its conjugate is not an independent field. The operators $D_M$ and $F_{MN}$ below are the covariant derivatives and curvature obtained by dimensional reduction of the ten-dimensional connection, with the mass twist in the 0 direction specified below.

The hypermultiplet has real Euclidean mass $m_E$ of mass dimension one, supplied by a nondynamical background flavor-vector multiplet whose fields are fixed and not integrated. In the source's orthonormal basis of the four hypermultiplet scalar directions, set $M_{ij}=i m_EJ_{ij}$, where $J$ is a real antisymmetric self-dual endomorphism of the oriented $i=5,\ldots,8$ space, $J^2=-I$, and $J_{ij}J^{ij}=4$. Thus $M$ is imaginary, antisymmetric, and self-dual, as required by the source. This is the N=2* deformation; $m_E=0$ is its N=4 limit. Its Scherk--Schwarz twist is

$$D_0\Phi_i=[\Phi_0,\Phi_i]+M_{ij}\Phi_j,\qquad D_0\Psi=[\Phi_0,\Psi]+\frac14M_{ij}\Gamma^{ij}\Psi.$$

For $D_\mu$, use the Levi-Civita derivative on spacetime/spin indices and the gauge covariant derivative $\nabla_\mu^A X=\nabla_\mu X+[A_\mu,X]$ on adjoint fields. In reduced scalar directions, $D_A X=[\Phi_A,X]$ before the displayed 0-direction twist. Define $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu+[A_\mu,A_\nu]$ and $F_{\mu A}=D_\mu\Phi_A$. Before the twist, $F_{AB}=[\Phi_A,\Phi_B]$; afterward, $F_{0i}=D_0\Phi_i$, $F_{i0}=-F_{0i}$, and the other reduced internal components retain their commutator values. The vector multiplet is neutral under this flavor twist. The fields have $[A_\mu]=[\Phi_A]=[m_E]=\mathrm{mass}$, $[\Psi]=\mathrm{mass}^{3/2}$, and $[K_a]=\mathrm{mass}^2$; the seven $K_a$ are smooth adjoint-valued scalars carrying the source's auxiliary $SO(7)$ index.

Let $R_{ij}$ be the source's real antisymmetric anti-self-dual matrix on the $i=5,\ldots,8$ scalar directions, normalized by $R_{ij}R^{ij}=4$. Adopt the source's curvature-coupled Scherk--Schwarz action

$$S_{\mathcal N=2^*}=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_{S^4_r}d^4x\sqrt g\,\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}\!\left(\frac12F_{MN}F^{MN}-\Psi\Gamma^MD_M\Psi+\frac{2}{r^2}\Phi_A\Phi^A-\frac{1}{4r}(R_{ki}M_{kj})\Phi^i\Phi^j-\sum_{a=1}^7K_aK_a\right).$$

Here $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$ is dimensionless, repeated ten-dimensional indices use the source's $(9,1)$ reduction metric before Euclidean continuation, and the trace is in the defining representation. In particular its four-dimensional gauge term is

$$S_{\mathrm{YM}}=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_{S^4_r}d^4x\sqrt g\,(F_{\mu\nu},F^{\mu\nu}).$$

The displayed $S_{\mathcal N=2^*}$ is the local curvature-coupled action; the theta angle $\theta$ is real and dimensionless and enters the source's sector weights. The source's sector-weight convention is

$$\tau=\frac{4\pi i}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}+\frac{\theta}{2\pi},\qquad q=e^{2\pi i\tau},$$

so a positive-instanton sector with formal label $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ carries weight $q^k$, and the corresponding anti-instanton factor uses $\bar q^{\,k}$ on the physical real slice. This adopts the source's convention without classifying bundle sectors or constructing the path-integral measure.

The rigid background is the fixed round metric and spin structure, the trivial $SU(2)_R$ background bundle with zero connection, the mass background, and a nonzero smooth conformal Killing-spinor pair $(\epsilon,\widetilde\epsilon)$ satisfying

$$\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\widetilde\Gamma_\mu\widetilde\epsilon,\qquad \nabla_\mu\widetilde\epsilon=-\frac{1}{4r^2}\Gamma_\mu\epsilon.$$

Choose the source's N=2 projection $\Gamma_{5678}\epsilon=\epsilon$, the source's constant-unit-norm solution, and $\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$. Use the same anti-self-dual matrix $R_{ij}$ as in the action to set $\Lambda=\frac14\Gamma^{ij}R_{ij}$, normalized by $\Lambda^2=-I$; the selected spinor pair satisfies $\widetilde\epsilon=\frac{1}{2r}\Lambda\epsilon$. Choose seven smooth auxiliary spinors $\nu_a$, $a=1,\ldots,7$, in the source's chiral spinor bundle satisfying

$$\epsilon\Gamma^M\nu_a=0,\qquad \frac12(\epsilon\Gamma_N\epsilon)\widetilde\Gamma^N_{\alpha\beta}=\sum_{a=1}^7\nu^a_\alpha\nu^a_\beta+\epsilon_\alpha\epsilon_\beta,\qquad \nu^a\Gamma^M\nu^b=\delta^{ab}\epsilon\Gamma^M\epsilon.$$

The selected supersymmetry transformation $s=\delta_\epsilon$ on the reduced physical and auxiliary fields is

$$sA_M=\Psi\Gamma_M\epsilon,\qquad s\Psi=\frac12\Gamma^{MN}F_{MN}\epsilon+\frac12\Gamma^{\mu A}\Phi_A\nabla_\mu\epsilon+\sum_{a=1}^7K_a\nu_a,\qquad sK_a=-\nu_a\Gamma^M D_M\Psi.$$

These are the off-shell transformations for this one selected generator; the finite set $K_a$ does not assert off-shell closure of the full N=2 hypermultiplet algebra. Their closure on the auxiliaries is

$$s^2K_a=-(\epsilon\Gamma^M\epsilon)D_MK_a-\sum_{b=1}^7(\nu_{[a}\Gamma^M D_M\nu_{b]})K_b-4(\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon)K_a.$$

Use the bilinear in exactly the source's order,
$$R^Q_{AB}=2\epsilon\widetilde\Gamma_{AB}\widetilde\epsilon,\qquad (\delta_R\Phi)_A=R^Q_{AB}\Phi^B,\qquad \delta_R\Psi=\tfrac14R^Q_{AB}\Gamma^{AB}\Psi.$$
Indices are raised with the reduction metric. The fixed normalized matrix $R_{ij}$ entering the mass action and $\Lambda$ above is distinguished from this dimensionful supercharge-square matrix $R^Q$. No interchange of $\epsilon$ and $\widetilde\epsilon$ is used: the stated transpose relation instead gives $2\widetilde\epsilon\Gamma_{AB}\epsilon=-R^Q_{AB}$. The source square is $s^2=-\mathscr L_v^{\mathrm{cov}}-\delta_R-\delta_\Omega-\delta_M$, with $v^M=\epsilon\Gamma^M\epsilon$, and $\delta_\Omega=0$ because $\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$. Here $\mathscr L_v^{\mathrm{cov}}$ already contains the gauge connection: on an adjoint scalar $X$ it is $v^\mu D_\mu X+[v^A\Phi_A,X]$, on the connection it is $\iota_vF_A-D_A(v^A\Phi_A)$, and on spinors it includes the geometric spin lift. The positive-sign mass operator is $\delta_M\Phi_i=v^0M_{ij}\Phi_j$ and $\delta_M\chi=\tfrac14v^0M_{ij}\Gamma^{ij}\chi$ on the adjoint hypermultiplet Dirac fermion $\chi$, and zero on the vector multiplet; consequently $-\delta_M$ gives exactly Pestun (2.25).

For a chosen sector, supply a one-parameter principal-bundle lift of the base flow and its induced spin lift, and let $\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}$ denote its infinitesimal pullback. In a local gauge frame write its vertical coefficient as $\beta_{v,P}$, so on adjoint scalars $\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}X=v^\mu\partial_\mu X+[\beta_{v,P},X]$, and on connections $\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}A=\mathcal L_v A-D_A\beta_{v,P}$. The difference $\mu_{v,A}=v^\mu A_\mu-\beta_{v,P}$ is a global adjoint section. Set $\kappa_v=\mu_{v,A}+v^A\Phi_A$ and $\phi=-\kappa_v$, and use $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)X=[u,X]$, $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A=-D_Au$. Then
$$\mathscr L_v^{\mathrm{cov}}=\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}+\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\kappa_v),\qquad s^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}-\delta_R-\delta_M.$$
On scalars the vertical coefficients add to $v^\mu A_\mu+v^A\Phi_A$; on connections, $\mathcal L_v A-D_A(v^\mu A_\mu+v^A\Phi_A)=\iota_vF_A-D_A(v^A\Phi_A)$. This explicitly reconciles the split with Pestun's gauge-covariant Lie derivative, rather than counting a gauge action twice. The auxiliary bundle is a rank-seven real orthogonal bundle tensored with $\operatorname{ad}P$; its combined spin/flavor/index lift is fixed by the displayed exact formula for $s^2K_a$. Equivalently its nongauge generator is $\omega K_a=s^2K_a-[\phi,K_a]$, with $s^2K_a$ exactly as above; a further independent scalar $R^Q$ or hypermultiplet $M_{ij}$ action is not added to its seven index labels. In this formula $D_\mu K_a=\partial_\mu K_a+[A_\mu,K_a]$ and $D_AK_a=[\Phi_A,K_a]$; the auxiliary flavor rotation is placed in the index matrix rather than added to $D_0K_a$. On the gauge-singlet background spinors set $D_\mu\nu_a=\nabla_\mu\nu_a$, $D_0\nu_a=\tfrac14M_{ij}\Gamma^{ij}\nu_a$ and $D_A\nu_a=0$ in the other reduced directions. This allocation follows directly from the mass term in $sK_a=-\nu_a\Gamma^MD_M\Psi$: its $K_b$ contribution on applying $s$ again is $-\tfrac14\nu_a\Gamma^0M_{ij}\Gamma^{ij}\nu_b K_b$, the antisymmetric auxiliary-index rotation encoded by $\nu_{[a}\Gamma^0D_0\nu_{b]}$. It fixes the induced auxiliary action even when the background spinors vary, without assigning the four-dimensional hypermultiplet index range to the seven auxiliaries. The spacetime component $v^\mu$ rotates the two orthogonal coordinate planes with equal angular magnitudes $r^{-1}$, so $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=r^{-1}$ at the poles. These sectorwise lifts are formal model inputs, not existence theorems for arbitrary bundles.

For gauge fixing in each declared sector, choose a lift-invariant background connection $A_*$, set $a=A-A_*\in\Omega^1(S^4,\operatorname{ad}P)$, and use the background slice $d_{A_*}^*a=0$, with Faddeev–Popov operator $d_{A_*}^*D_A$ on smooth adjoint-valued scalar sections. Let $G$ be a complex affine algebraic group acting algebraically on a classical
variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-rational-action-on-affine-variety]]). A $G$-invariant morphism
$\pi:X\to Y$ is a **categorical quotient** if every $G$-invariant morphism
$f:X\to Z$ of classical varieties factors uniquely as $f=\varphi\circ\pi$ with
$\varphi:Y\to Z$ a morphism.

It is a **geometric quotient** (Brion Definition 1.18) if

(i) $\pi$ is surjective and its fibres are exactly the $G$-orbits,

(ii) a subset $U\subseteq Y$ is open if and only if $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is open in
$X$, and

(iii) for every open $U\subseteq Y$ the pullback of regular functions is an
isomorphism $\mathcal O_Y(U)\to\mathcal O_X(\pi^{-1}(U))^G$ onto the
$G$-invariant regular functions on the preimage.

A geometric quotient is a categorical quotient and is unique up to unique
isomorphism; when it exists its underlying topological space is the orbit space
$X/G$ with the quotient topology. For an affine $G$-variety $X$ whose invariant
algebra $\mathbb C[X]^G$ is finitely generated, the affine model is the morphism
$\pi:X\to X/\!/G:=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[X]^G$ induced by the inclusion
$\mathbb C[X]^G\subseteq\mathbb C[X]$. For a reductive $G$, the theorem below
proves this finite generation and makes the model a categorical quotient with
one closed orbit in each fibre
([[thm-invariant-ring-finite-generation-and-affine-categorical-quotient]]).

**Why a geometric quotient is categorical.** Let $\pi:X\to Y$ satisfy (i)–(iii)
and let $f:X\to Z$ be a $G$-invariant morphism to a classical variety $Z$. By
(i) two points of a fibre of $\pi$ lie in one orbit, on which $f$ is constant,
so $f$ factors through a unique set map $\bar f:Y\to Z$. For $W\subseteq Z$
open, $\pi^{-1}(\bar f^{-1}(W))=f^{-1}(W)$ is open in $X$ by continuity of $f$,
so $\bar f^{-1}(W)$ is open in $Y$ by (ii): $\bar f$ is continuous. If $V$ is an
affine chart of $Z$ with coordinates $s$ and $U:=\bar f^{-1}(V)$, then
$s\circ f$ is a $G$-invariant regular function on $\pi^{-1}(U)$, hence by (iii)
is the pullback along $\pi$ of a unique regular function on $U$; that function
is $s\circ\bar f$. Since this holds for every coordinate $s$ of an affine chart,
$\bar f$ is a morphism
([[def-classical-affine-variety-morphism]],
[[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and local
agreement of the resulting morphisms on overlapping charts gives a morphism
$Y\to Z$. Surjectivity in (i) makes the factorisation unique. If also
$\pi':X\to Y'$ is a categorical quotient, the universal property applied to
$\pi'$ and to $\pi$ yields morphisms $\varphi:Y\to Y'$ with $\varphi\pi=\pi'$
and $\psi:Y'\to Y$ with $\psi\pi'=\pi$; then $(\varphi\psi)\pi'=\pi'$ and
$(\psi\varphi)\pi=\pi$, so uniqueness of the factorisation of $\pi'$ through
$\pi'$ and of $\pi$ through $\pi$ forces $\varphi\psi=\operatorname{id}_{Y'}$
and $\psi\varphi=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Thus categorical and geometric
quotients are unique up to unique isomorphism, and for a geometric quotient
(i)–(ii) say exactly that the underlying map is the quotient map of the orbit
equivalence relation with the quotient topology.

**Conventions.** This is the classical notion of Brion Definition 1.18 and the
paragraph after Theorem 1.24. The scheme-theoretic fppf quotient sheaf on the
AG-ACT-1 page is a different object and is not identified with this classical
notion here. In the classical register, $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a finitely
generated reduced complex algebra denotes its associated affine variety of
complex closed points with the classical regular-function sheaf; no
identification with the space of every scheme prime is used. For empty $X$ the
coordinate algebra is zero and its quotient is empty; finite generation and the
universal properties below are then immediate and fibre assertions are vacuous.
The definition itself uses no Axiom of Choice; the finite-generation theorem
referred to above inherits AC from its own named suppliers, so consumers of that
theorem carry AC, while nothing in this definition does.

Assume AC. Let $E\to B$ be a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle with $n\geq1$
over a path-connected CW complex $B$ (or over one of the CW-type bases of
[[thm-integral-complex-projective-bundle-theorem]]). By that theorem there are
unique classes $a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)$, $1\leq i\leq n$, such that
$$x_E^{\,n}-a_1x_E^{\,n-1}+a_2x_E^{\,n-2}-\cdots+(-1)^na_n=0\qquad\text{in }H^{2n}(P(E);\mathbb Z),$$
where $x_E\in H^2(P(E);\mathbb Z)$ is the Euler class of the underlying real
bundle of the tautological line
([[def-complex-projective-bundle-and-tautological-complex-line]]). The
**Chern classes** of $E$ are these coefficients:
$$c_i(E):=a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)\qquad(1\leq i\leq n),$$
completed by the conventions $c_0(E):=1\in H^0(B;\mathbb Z)$ and
$c_i(E):=0$ for $i>n$, and the **total Chern class** is the finite sum
$c(E):=\sum_{i\geq0}c_i(E)=1+c_1(E)+\cdots+c_n(E)\in H^*(B;\mathbb Z)$.

For the zero bundle of rank $0$ the conventions give $c(0_B)=1$. The definition
depends only on the isomorphism class of $E$, because an isomorphism of
bundles induces an isomorphism of projective bundles pulling $x$ back to $x$
and hence preserves the unique relation. For a complex line bundle $L\to B$ one
has $P(L)\cong B$ over $B$ with $\gamma_L$ corresponding to $L$ under that
identification, so the relation is $x_L-c_1(L)=0$; since $x_L=e(L_{\mathbb R})$
under the identification, this gives
$$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R}).$$
This is the normalization used throughout the page: the first Chern class of a
complex line is the Euler class of its underlying real bundle in the complex
orientation, not a separately chosen normalization.

$\xi\to B$ be an $R$-oriented numerable real rank-$n$ vector bundle over a
base in the scope of that theorem. Let $u_\xi\in H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$ be its
normalized Thom class, let
$$j^*:H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)\longrightarrow H^n(D(\xi);R)$$ be the relative-to-absolute map of the pair sequence, and let $s:B\to D(\xi)$ be the zero section. The **Euler class** of $\xi$ is $$e(\xi)=e_{\rm Th}(\xi):=s^*j^*(u_\xi)\in H^n(B;R).$$
This is the class already introduced in
[[def-thom-euler-class-of-an-oriented-vector-bundle]]: on this page we write
$e(\xi)$ for it, and the shorthand $s^*u_\xi$ always means the composite
$s^*j^*(u_\xi)$, the relative-to-absolute map being understood. For rank zero
with supplied orientation $o\in H^0(B;R)$, normalization gives $u_\xi=o$ and
$j$ and $s$ are identities, so
$$e(0_B,o)=o\in H^0(B;R).$$
In particular, the standard unit orientation gives $e(0_B,1)=1$.
For $R=\mathbb F_2$ every real bundle is canonically $\mathbb F_2$-oriented by
[[def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system]], so in that
case $e_2(\xi):=e(\xi)\in H^n(B;\mathbb F_2)$ is defined for every real
bundle in the Thom scope; for $R=\mathbb Z$ the class depends on the chosen
integral orientation, and reversing the orientation negates it.

$E\to B$ and $F\to B$ be $R$-oriented numerable real bundles of ranks $m,n\geq0$

$e(E),e(F)$. The coefficient ring $R$ is commutative and unital.
Every rank-zero input carries the standard unit orientation; the orientation
reversal assertion below applies only in positive rank. Both bases in a
pullback square are required to lie in the general Thom scope.

1. **Naturality.** For an orientation-preserving pullback square

   $$
   \begin{CD} f^*E @>>> E\\ @VVV @VVV\\ B' @>f>> B\end{CD}
   $$
   one has $e(f^*E)=f^*e(E)$.
2. **Orientation sign.** Over $R=\mathbb Z$ and $m>0$, reversing the orientation of $E$
   negates the class: $e(E,-o)=-e(E,o)$.
3. **Whitney product.** Give $E\oplus F$ the ordered direct-sum orientation.
   Then $e(E\oplus F)=e(E)e(F)$, including the rank-zero unit $e(0_B)=1$.
4. **Koszul sign.** The swap $E\oplus F\to F\oplus E$ changes the ordered-sum
   orientation by $(-1)^{mn}$. Consequently the Euler products in the two

   $$e(E)e(F)=(-1)^{mn}e(F)e(E).$$

Then
$$

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$ and a real stability parameter $\zeta>0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with Hermitian structures, and let $\mathcal S_{k,N}^\zeta$ be the locus of quadruples $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$, satisfying $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and the condition that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$ for all words of length $m\geq0$ and $w\in W$. The group $GL(V)$ acts algebraically by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. These are algebraic coordinates on the finite-dimensional complex data space; this formal quotient assigns no spacetime units to $B_i,I,J$. The parameter $\zeta$ labels the positive stability chamber and is not assigned a physical dimension here. Let $\pi_{k,N}:\mathcal S_{k,N}^\zeta\to X_{k,N}^\zeta$ be the positive-FI geometric quotient in the classical variety sense: $\pi_{k,N}$ is a surjective invariant morphism whose fibres are precisely the $GL(V)$-orbits; $U\subseteq X_{k,N}^\zeta$ is open exactly when $\pi_{k,N}^{-1}(U)$ is open; and for every such $U$ pullback identifies $\mathcal O_{X_{k,N}^\zeta}(U)$ with $\mathcal O_{\mathcal S_{k,N}^\zeta}(\pi_{k,N}^{-1}(U))^{GL(V)}$. Under the stable positive-FI hypotheses, the supplied stable ADHM quotient result gives this quotient a separated smooth finite-type complex structure of dimension $2kN$ and a finite invariant affine word-slice atlas. The parameter $\zeta$ labels the positive stability chamber; this is not, by definition, the zero-FI regular quotient or the moduli space of anti-self-dual connections.

Let $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^\times)^2\times(\mathbb C^\times)^N$ act algebraically, and let $K=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ be its maximal compact subgroup. The action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Thus $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. Write $\epsilon_i=c_1^K(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^K(e_\alpha)$; each has mass dimension one in units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $q$ be a dimensionless formal charge-counting variable.

Assume the complexified torus action has a finite proper fixed locus $F_{k,N}$ on each quotient. Extend the torus to $T_m=T_{\mathbb C}\times\mathbb C_m^\times$ with maximal compact subgroup $K_m=K\times S_m^1$; the flavor factor acts trivially on $X_{k,N}^\zeta$. Use the product right Milnor model $E K_m$, and write $B K_m=E K_m/K_m$ and $X_{k,N,K_m}^\zeta=E K_m\times_{K_m}X_{k,N}^\zeta$, with diagonal quotient relation $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$. Equivariant cohomology means $H_{T_m}^*(X_{k,N}^\zeta;\mathbb Q)=H^*(X_{k,N,K_m}^\zeta;\mathbb Q)$. The derivative action makes $TX_{k,N}^\zeta$ a $K_m$-equivariant complex vector bundle, and its Borel descent is $E K_m\times_{K_m}TX_{k,N}^\zeta\to X_{k,N,K_m}^\zeta$. Assume each component of this Borel base has CW type and that the descended bundle, including its tensor products below, is numerable; Chern classes are formed componentwise on a CW model and transported by homotopy invariance. For a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle $E$ on a connected CW model, its Chern classes are the unique coefficients in the projective-bundle relation $x_E^n-c_1(E)x_E^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^nc_n(E)=0$, where $P(E)$ is the bundle of complex lines in the fibers and $x_E=c_1(\gamma_E)$ for the tautological line $\gamma_E\to P(E)$. We use their rational images. For a character $\chi:T_m\to\mathbb C^\times$, let $L_\chi=E K_m\times_{K_m}\mathbb C_{\chi|_{K_m}}\to B K_m$ be its associated line, with right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$, and write $u_\chi=c_1(L_\chi)$. Put $\widetilde m=u_{\chi_m}$ for the defining flavor character, of mass dimension one like $\epsilon_i$ and $a_\alpha$, and let $L_{-1}=L_{\chi_m^{-1}}$; thus its additive weight is $-\widetilde m$. At a fixed point with tangent characters $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_{2kN}$ and additive weights $w_j=u_{\chi_j}$, pullback to $B K_m$ gives character lines $L_{\chi_j\chi_m^{-1}}$. The top Chern class of a rank-$n$ complex bundle equals the Euler class of its complex-oriented real bundle, and the Euler class is natural and multiplicative for ordered direct sums; for a character line its Euler class is its first Chern class. Therefore the top Chern restriction is $\prod_{j=1}^{2kN}(w_j-\widetilde m)$.

Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.
